name: STAGE PIANO
play: Piano remains the foreground instrument. Use three- or four-note voicings; the three quiet mono supports colour the last played note while the main piano stays polyphonic. This is a synthesized stage piano, not a sampled acoustic grand.

name: VELVET EP
play: Rhodes-style electric piano leads. The warm polyphonic undertone follows the chords; the quiet mono tine and upper harmonic supports add articulation. Use up to three-note voicings.

name: COPPER LEAD
play: A singing monophonic synth lead with quiet octave sheen, FM edge and a short modal accent. Use a single-note melody; wheel or pressure adds vibrato.

name: ORIENT LEAD
play: Mizmar-style reed leads, with quiet Shabi saw, ney breath and a plucked accent. Starts in equal temperament; select your maqam and root explicitly. All parts follow master tuning by default.

name: DISCO POLY
play: Punchy poly-synth keys are dominant. Use rhythmic three- or four-note stabs; short mono brass and organ accents add definition without taking four voices per chord note.

name: BRASS STACK
play: A bold synth-brass section with lower-octave body, FM bite and upper string attack. Use open two- or three-note voicings.

name: SILK STRINGS
play: An ensemble string sound stays in front. The second polyphonic string layer blends below it; mono cello and choir supply quiet body and air. Use open two- or three-note voicings.

name: NEON BASS
play: The centred analogue bass is the main instrument. Pulse definition, a quiet upper-octave vector layer and a plucked edge support it. All four parts are monophonic.
